**Proof.**

Let $f = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{1}_{A_n}$. Since each $\mathbb{1}_{A_n}$ is measurable, $f$ is a non-negative measurable function, so $\int_X f\,d\mu$ is well-defined (in $[0,\infty]$).

**Step 1. Identify the set where $f = 1$.**

For $x \in X$, we have $f(x) = 1$ if and only if $x \in A_n$ for infinitely many $n$, i.e.,
$$\{x \in X : f(x) = 1\} = \limsup_{n \to \infty} A_n = \bigcap_{N=1}^{\infty}\bigcup_{n \ge N} A_n.$$
On the complement, $f(x) = 0$. Thus $f = \mathbb{1}_{\limsup A_n}$, and
$$\int_X f\,d\mu = \mu\!\left(\limsup_{n \to \infty} A_n\right).$$

**Step 2. Bound the measure of the limsup.**

For every $N \in \mathbb{N}$,
$$\limsup_{n \to \infty} A_n \subseteq \bigcup_{n \ge N} A_n,$$
so by subadditivity and the hypothesis $\sum_{n} \mu(A_n) < \infty$,
$$\mu\!\left(\limsup_{n \to \infty} A_n\right) \le \mu\!\left(\bigcup_{n \ge N} A_n\right) \le \sum_{n \ge N} \mu(A_n).$$

Since the series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \mu(A_n)$ converges, its tail tends to zero:
$$\sum_{n \ge N} \mu(A_n) \xrightarrow{N \to \infty} 0.$$

**Step 3. Conclude.**

The bound $\mu(\limsup A_n) \le \sum_{n \ge N} \mu(A_n)$ holds for every $N$, and the right-hand side can be made arbitrarily small. Therefore
$$\mu\!\left(\limsup_{n \to \infty} A_n\right) = 0.$$
Consequently,
$$\int_X \limsup_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{1}_{A_n}\,d\mu = \mu\!\left(\limsup_{n \to \infty} A_n\right) = 0. \qquad \blacksquare$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
